definition.value: F-SCORE, the sum of nine binary financial-performance signals measuring profitability, leverage/liquidity, and operating efficiency.

evidence.quote: I define the aggregate signal measure, F-SCORE, as the sum of the nine binary signals.

economic_intuition.value: A higher F-SCORE identifies financially stronger high book-to-market firms whose historical financial information indicates better future performance and returns.

evidence.quote: To the extent current fundamentals predict future fundamentals, I expect F-SCORE to be positively associated with changes in future firm performance and stock returns.

formula.paper_expression: F-SCORE = F_ROA + F_AROA + F_CFO + F_ACCRUAL + F_AMARGIN + F_ATURN + F_ALEVER + F_ALIQUID + EQOFFER.

steps.description: Calculate return on assets as net income before extraordinary items scaled by beginning-of-year total assets.

evidence.quote: I define ROA and CFO as net income before extraordinary items and cash flow from operations, respectively, scaled by beginning-of-the-year total assets.

steps.description: Calculate cash flow from operations scaled by beginning-of-year total assets.

evidence.quote: I define ROA and CFO as net income before extraordinary items and cash flow from operations, respectively, scaled by beginning-of-the-year total assets.

steps.description: Assign one when ROA is positive and zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: If the firm's ROA (CFO) is positive, I define the indicator variable F_ROA (F_CFO) equal to one, zero otherwise.

steps.description: Assign one when CFO is positive and zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: If the firm's ROA (CFO) is positive, I define the indicator variable F_ROA (F_CFO) equal to one, zero otherwise.

steps.description: Assign one when current ROA exceeds prior-year ROA and zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: I define AROA as the current year's ROA less the prior year's ROA. If AROA > 0, the indicator variable F-AROA equals one, zero otherwise.

steps.description: Assign one when CFO exceeds ROA and zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: The indicator variable F_ACCRUAL equals one if CFO > ROA, zero otherwise.

steps.description: Assign one when the long-term-debt-to-average-assets ratio falls from the prior year and zero otherwise.
steps.expression: indicator((long_term_debt + debt_current) / average(total_assets, lag(total_assets, 1)) < lag((long_term_debt + debt_current) / average(total_assets, lag(total_assets, 1)), 1))

evidence.quote: I define the indicator variable F_ALEVER as equal to one (zero) if the firm's leverage ratio fell (rose) in the year preceding portfolio formation.

steps.description: Assign one when the current ratio increases from the prior year and zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: The indicator variable F_ALIQUID equals one if the firm's liquidity improved, zero otherwise.

steps.description: Assign one when the firm did not issue common equity in the year preceding portfolio formation and zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: I define the indicator variable EQOFFER as equal to one if the firm did not issue common equity in the year preceding portfolio formation, zero otherwise.

steps.description: Assign one when gross margin divided by sales increases from the prior year and zero otherwise.
steps.expression: indicator((net_sales - cost_of_goods_sold) / net_sales > lag((net_sales - cost_of_goods_sold) / net_sales, 1))

evidence.quote: The indicator variable F-AMARGIN equals one if AAMARGIN is positive, zero otherwise.

steps.description: Assign one when sales divided by average total assets increases from the prior year and zero otherwise.
steps.expression: indicator(net_sales / average(total_assets, lag(total_assets, 1)) > lag(net_sales / average(total_assets, lag(total_assets, 1)), 1))

evidence.quote: I define A TURN as the firm's current year asset turnover ratio (total sales scaled by beginning-of-the-year total assets) less the prior year's asset turnover ratio.
ATURN= change in the firm's asset turnover ratio between the end of year t and year t - 1. The asset turnover ratio is defined as net sales scaled by average total assets for the year.

steps.description: Sum the nine binary financial-performance indicators.
steps.expression: f_roa + f_aroa + f_cfo + f_accrual + f_amargin + f_aturn + f_alever + f_aliquid + f_eqoffer

evidence.quote: I define F-SCORE as the sum of the individual binary signals.
Given the nine underlying signals, F-SCORE can range from a low of 0 to a high of 9.
Each fiscal year (i.e., financial report year), I rank all firms.
I measure firm-specific returns as one-year (two-year) buy-and-hold returns.
Each year between 1976 and 1996, I identify firms with sufficient stock price and book value data on Compustat.
Return compounding ends the earlier of one year (two years) after return compounding began or the last day of CRSP traded returns.

formation_rule.value: Form portfolios at the beginning of the fifth month after fiscal year-end, using annual financial information.

evidence.quote: I chose the fifth month to ensure that the necessary annual financial information is available to investors at the time of portfolio formation.
Each fiscal year (i.e., financial report year), I rank all firms.
A raw return is calculated as the 12-month buy-and-hold return of the firm starting at the beginning of the fifth month after fiscal year-end.
Returns are cumulated over a one-year period starting four months after fiscal year-end.

The primary methodology of this paper is to form portfolios based on the firm's aggregate score (F-SCORE).
I classify firms with the lowest aggregate signals (F-SCORE equals 0 or 1) as low F-SCORE firms.
evidence.interpretation: A single sort is conducted on F-SCORE.

evidence.quote: firms receiving the highest score (i.e., F-SCORE equals 8 or 9) have the strongest fundamental signals and are classified as high F-SCORE firms.
I classify firms with the lowest aggregate signals (F-SCORE equals 0 or 1) as low F-SCORE firms.
evidence.interpretation: Thresholds are applied to retained high-BM firms, not an exchange-specific reference subset.

evidence.quote: The Low F-SCORE portfolio consists of firms with an aggregate score of 0 or 1; the High FSCORE portfolio consists of firms with a score of 8 or 9.

notes: This specification targets the paper's primary binary F-SCORE strategy: high book-to-market firms with F-SCORE 8 or 9 versus those with F-SCORE 0 or 1. The paper also reports alternative ranked-signal and annual majority-good-versus-majority-bad variants, which are separate executable targets and are not merged into this specification.
